title: Add score-per-dollar models to articles and value-frontier visual
Produce visuals for the three AI-coding-economics articles
description:
19 visual placeholders are now in place across the three draft articles, each paired with an MDX comment holding a paste-ready prompt or chart spec.

1. Three poster heroes (magenta stencil; oxblood variant for bugonomics) - these replace obvious placeholder cards and are the social preview images
2. agentjacking-chain.svg (PlantUML) and value-frontier.png (matplotlib) - the definitive visual for each article
3. two-multiplying-curves.png and break-even-crossing.png - each draws an argument prose currently carries alone
4. robot-workstation-army.png (photoreal)
5. Remainder: cache-economics, same-curve-both-directions, 500k-to-14-funnel, trying-every-door, the-backlog-worked, plus the no-asset HTML components (fast-tier comparisonChart, context snowball blockDiagram, three-tier comparisonChart, LiL taxonomy panels)

Toolchains already present: matplotlib house style matches src/blog/images/classifiers/ and turn-detection charts; PlantUML via 'bundle exec plantuml_diagrams process -i src/blog/diagrams -o ./'.

BLOCKING ACCEPTANCE CRITERIA: before ANY of the three articles flips to state: published, remove every .visualPlaceholder block from the three MDX files AND the .blockDiagram.visualPlaceholder rule from src/components/layout.scss. The placeholders render publicly on draft pages.

comments.author: Ryan Alyn Porter
comments.text:
2023 profit chart placeholder RESOLVED - real image now rendering.

- Added ./images/classifiers/profit_per_million_GPT-4_GPT-3.5_Ada_2_BERT.png to the article's images: frontmatter (resolves via @fileByRelativePath; same relative base as the 2023 article since both live in src/blog/)
- Replaced the placeholder block with a real BlogImage + framing prose
- Verified rendering: no 'No image found for' fallback; chart happens to be in brand magenta and sits well

Note on BlogImage: it does NOT use the images prop for lookup. It runs a global allFile query and matches on relativePath.endsWith(name), so any sourced image resolves by basename alone. The frontmatter entry was added anyway for explicitness and in case that lookup is ever tightened.

Placeholders remaining in this article: 6 (was 7).

ALSO FIXED while verifying:
- Table CSS: font-size was a fixed token rendering at roughly half the surrounding body copy; now 0.9em so it tracks the article, plus an explicit color: var(--color-text).
- Table alignment: GFM emits Markdown column alignment as an 'align' attribute, which is only a presentational hint and loses to CSS text-align. My 'thead th { text-align: left }' was forcing every header left while the body cells honoured the attribute, so headers did not line up with their columns. Now scoped to th:not([align]) / td:not([align]) so authored alignment wins.
- Two factual errors in the article's own prose, caught by looking at the chart: the 2023 piece did NOT reject Word2Vec for falling below the accuracy bar (it hit 97% against a 95% requirement) - it was rejected because the accuracy drop was not worth a trivial training-time saving. Corrected the lede and the new chart caption accordingly.

comments.author: Ryan Alyn Porter
comments.text:
value-frontier.png revised, and a second chart (value-over-time.png) built and inserted -- both real, finished images now, not placeholders.

PROBLEM CAUGHT BY USER: the original value-frontier bar chart (Luna tallest, Sol shortest, left-to-right descending) visually reads as 'value declining' even though it's a same-moment model comparison, not a timeline -- directly contradicting the article's 'skyrocketing value' thesis on a skim.

FIX: built value-over-time.png, an ascending log-scale line chart, 1200x630, installed at src/blog/images/value-over-time.png. Placed at the end of 'The other half of the ratio' (the section that first makes the temporal claim), BEFORE 'There is a scoreboard now' where the snapshot bar chart lives -- so the ascending trend now leads and the bar chart is explicitly reframed as 'a single frame from it, not a timeline' in the prose immediately before it.

DATA SOURCE: no new claims. Baseline Feb 2025 ('vibe coding' coined) = 1x, compounding at the SAME already-cited, already-fact-checked rates from the companion article (ai-coding-cost-collapse-2026.mdx): SWE-bench-specific ~4.7x/yr -> ~10x by Aug 2026 (conservative line), and the broader MIT Price-of-Progress 5x-10x/yr band -> ~11x-32x (shaded band). Cites the same arXiv 2511.23455 paper already used earlier in this article.

ITERATION on the two milestone annotations (GLM 5.2 Jun 16 2026, Luna price cut Jul 30 2026), per user feedback across several rounds:
1. Initial inline labels collided (dates only 6 weeks apart)
2. Consolidated into a bottom-right footnote -- user found this still read as overlapping/unclear
3. Back to per-line labels, staggered vertically (rightward/Luna higher, per explicit instruction) -- a curved connector arrow across the log-scale y-axis distorted into a confusing arc, removed
4. FINAL: bare name + date only, rotated 90 deg, positioned directly beside each dashed vertical line, no arrows, no extra explanation. DeepSeek R1 dropped entirely (its Jan 20 2025 date falls before the Feb 2025 chart start).

Frontmatter images: array updated with both value-over-time.png and value-frontier.png.

ENVIRONMENT NOTE: disk repeatedly filled to under 300MB free during this work, purely from gatsby develop + webpack cache, unrelated to file sizes involved. Reclaimed via rm -rf .cache/public four times this session. Left the dev server stopped at end of session for that reason -- restart with npm start (or the anthus-dev preview config) before the next round of work, and expect to reclaim cache again if it fills.

title: Add task management as multi-agent coordination infrastructure
description: Task management systems like Taskulus/Beads enable stepping back from pair programming to manager/delegator role. Without them, you're stuck in interactive sessions. With them, you can delegate to multiple agents like managing contractors. This is critical infrastructure for scaling beyond 1:1 chat interactions.
notes: Added 'Task Management: From Pair Programming to Delegation' subsection in WIP section. Explains how task management systems enable scaling from interactive chat to parallel delegation across multiple agents. Links to Taskulus and Beads. Committed in 444004f.

title: Fix: global table CSS leaked into custom table components
description:
RESOLVED in the same session - recording for history.

The bare 'table' selectors added to src/components/layout.scss when GFM was enabled leaked into two pre-existing hand-authored table components: 'article table.data' and '.blockDiagram .messages'. Those declare their own border-collapse/padding/colors and win on specificity, but do NOT declare display, white-space, overflow-x, border-bottom or vertical-align - so the new rules applied to those properties. Below the 720px breakpoint 'display: block' and 'white-space: nowrap' visibly broke both components.

Affected and deployed: how-ai-agents-do-things, how-ai-agents-know-things, rethinking-ai-hallucination, langchain-by-example, the-dominance-of-ones.

Fix: scoped every rule via a $md-table SCSS variable to 'table:not(.data):not(.messages)'.

Verified at 375px (the width where the break showed): .messages and table.data both compute display:table / white-space:normal; .blockDiagram.request keeps its blue; GFM tables still scroll within themselves and the page does not overflow horizontally.

title: Fix fabricated product references in cybernetic-development
description:
Two fabricated product references found and fixed on feature/homepage-2026-positioning, both shadowing real Anthus products. Same failure mode as the three fabricated citations found earlier in bugonomics.

1. 'Tactus' was used as a prompt-to-app strawman the article argued against, while the real Tactus is the Anthus DSL for durable agent procedures -- an example of the Agents-as-Code tier the article argues FOR. Replaced with the category ('Prompt-to-App Generators', illustrated with Lovable and Bolt.new, both verified) and Tactus added back as a positive example, scoped honestly since its README says alpha.

2. 'Taskulus' did not exist at all -- no repo, absent from the anthus-footer registry, and the cited URL https://taskul.us/architecture was invented. The code examples settled what it actually was: the Gherkin scenario asserts a project/issues directory, which is how Kanbus stores issues in this very repo. Retargeted to Kanbus throughout including tsk init -> kanbus init and TaskulusWorld -> KanbusWorld, citation repointed at kanb.us/architecture. NOTE: not Virtuus, which shares the Gherkin-as-source methodology but is a table engine, not an issue tracker.

Audited the other 16 citations: all verified (the $57K Cursor claim and its framing, both Karpathy status IDs, Lee Robinson, and the Ashby/Kahneman/Reason/Jevons/Goodhart/Kasparov/Stephenson/Spolsky/PARC references). Two corrections: the Better Programming piece is by Anna Geller (author field held the publication name, and the 2017 date was Vogels's re:Invent year), and Lee Robinson's migration took three days not 'a weekend'.

Article also flipped to state: published, dated 2026-08-18, which unblocks the homepage merge.

title: AGENTS.md contradicts itself: Beads vs Kanbus
description:
Root AGENTS.md line ~404 says 'Beads task management is MANDATORY here; every task must live in Beads' and the Landing the Plane section says to run 'bd sync'. But project/AGENTS.md says 'Do not edit issues/ or events/ directly; use Kanbus for issues and events.'

Current state: bd is installed (/opt/homebrew/bin/bd) and .beads/ is tracked in git. kanbus is NOT on PATH, and project/issues/ + project/events/ + project/AGENTS.md + project/wiki/ are all UNTRACKED, so the Kanbus state is not versioned with the repo. Two Kanbus issues exist (cost-collapse article in_progress, bugonomics open) that duplicate Beads coverage.

An agent reading these instructions cannot tell which system is authoritative, and cannot use Kanbus at all without the CLI. Recommend picking one, updating both AGENTS.md files to agree, and either committing project/ or gitignoring it deliberately.

Surfaced when Ryan pointed out that project/ is this repo's project management state after I dismissed it as not-ours.
